purpose: Reference guide for AI-assisted brand font selection. It maps typeface styles to the brand personality they convey; it is independent of industry. The styles are practical design groupings, not rigid classifications. Check font licensing and language support before production use.
selection_guidelines: Match the brand personality, target audience, and intended media rather than choosing a font solely by industry.
Prefer fonts with Polish Latin characters when creating Polish-language material.
Verify legibility at small sizes, adequate weight options, and availability in the intended rendering environment.
A single font family can be sufficient for both headings and body text.
If mixing families, pair contrasting but compatible fonts and keep the system simple.
Treat the examples as suggestions, not mandatory choices. Confirm licensing before commercial deployment.

styles.description: Clean, structured typefaces with geometric letterforms; contemporary, approachable, and visually consistent.
styles.considerations: Some geometric faces are less comfortable for long passages; test body readability.

styles.description: Unobtrusive, highly legible typography designed to support information clarity and flexible interfaces.
styles.considerations: A neutral choice may need stronger color, layout, or imagery to feel distinctive.

styles.description: Open, organic letterforms that balance readability with warmth and personality.
styles.considerations: Choose weights carefully to avoid a generic corporate appearance.

styles.description: Soft shapes and rounded terminals create a playful, gentle, and welcoming impression.
styles.considerations: Highly rounded or playful faces can reduce perceived formality and may work better for headings than long body copy.

styles.description: Distinctive contrast between thick and thin strokes creates a refined, editorial, or luxurious look.
styles.considerations: Delicate strokes may suffer at small sizes; use strong contrast with the background and consider a simpler body face.

styles.description: Traditional serif structures associated with editorial depth, stability, and long-form reading.
styles.considerations: Serif designs vary substantially; verify on-screen rendering and the desired balance between traditional and modern.

styles.description: Expressive serifs that combine a literary or artisanal tone with a contemporary brand identity.
styles.considerations: Expressive shapes are useful for memorable headlines; check body legibility and available optical sizes.

styles.description: Letterforms inspired by everyday handwriting, suggesting spontaneity and personal connection.
styles.considerations: Best used sparingly for short headlines, notes, or accents; test Polish diacritics and avoid dense paragraphs.

styles.description: Flowing, calligraphic letterforms that suggest emotion, elegance, or celebration.
styles.considerations: Usually unsuitable for paragraphs and small UI labels; check accented glyph coverage for Polish text.

styles.description: High-impact typography intended to attract attention in short messages and large-format designs.
styles.considerations: Use primarily for headlines, slogans, and advertising. Condensed or all-caps typography needs spacing checks.

styles.description: Fixed-width letterforms with a systematic and technical feel.
styles.considerations: Use selectively in general marketing; long paragraphs can become visually dense.

styles.description: Nostalgic or characterful letterforms that evoke specific historical moods without requiring a strictly historical identity.
styles.considerations: The examples span different visual eras; assess the actual visual fit, not just the category label.

styles.description: Strong, block-like serifs create a sturdy, grounded, and memorable impression.
styles.considerations: The category ranges from neutral text fonts to bold display faces; verify commercial licensing for each chosen font.
